description: Codex round 9 P1: empirical probe of minimatch 3.1.5's `\X` handling. Reference behavior: `\X` is transparent — the backslash is effectively stripped and the meta-character keeps its glob meaning for X in `*`/`?`/`[`/`{`. The `\.` case (round 8) admits leading-dot paths because the de-escaped form starts with a literal `.`; the same de-escape uniformly applies to all glob meta characters but they retain their meta meaning when they're, well, meta. Locks the round-9 fix that reverted the round-8 over-generalization (`backslash_escape(true)` on globset which made `\*` literal-`*`).
